The *Hemakattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 409) is a Pali verse narrative included in the Therāpadāna division of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the spiritual aspirations and merit-making deeds of the elder (thera) Hemaka in past and present existences [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text in five languages, and notes cross-references or connections to the *Soṇakajātaka* (Ja 529), the *Todeyyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 410), and the *Bhaddālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 413) [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus identify substantial formulaic and textual overlap, recording 210 matching passages shared with 30 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The largest Pali partner is the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, first and second parts), containing 70 matches including an alignment of segment §18.3–21.4 with commentary prose [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares extended sequences with neighboring poems in the Therāpadāna, prominently the *Bhaddālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 413, where §25.1–30.4 matches §12.1–17.4), the *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 414), and the *Todeyyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 410), as well as verses in the *Mahājanakajātaka* (Ja 539) and the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language comparisons, DharmaNexus aligns segment §35.2 with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* from Subaši, alongside minor matches in the Chinese *Dāloutanjīng* (T 23) and Tibetan translations including the *Subhāṣitaratnakaraṇḍakakathā* (D4168) [DharmaNexus].
